{{Quote|This isn't Tatooine, Luke.|Leia Organa, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="hunt" />}}
'''Tirahnn''' was a bustling trade [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim's]] [[Zeemacht Cluster/Legends|Zeemacht Cluster]], that served as an important stop along the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]]. A mercantilist society essentially ruled by super-rich "merchant princes," Tirahnn was known across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for its massive bazaars and markets, the largest of which stretched for miles and were bigger than entire nations on other planets. This made Tirahnn a popular destination for rich tourists, with the annual [[Great Fair]] especially drawing a vast number of visitors to the world. Among the offworlders who stopped by for the Great Fair were famed [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] leaders [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], who visited the event in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. Tirahnn's importance as a trade nexus made it occasionally a target during wartime: during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] it changed hands multiple times between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].

==Description==
A major trade world along the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]], Tirahnn served as the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the<ref name="tt" /> [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim's]]<ref name="EAOC" /> [[Zeemacht Cluster/Legends|Zeemacht Cluster]]. Tirahnn's landscape was characterized by vast plains, [[Forest/Legends|forests]] and [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]]. The planet's weather was mild year-round, and much of Tirahnn remained pastoral millennia after civilization became widespread.<ref name="tt" /> Tirahnn's fields were filled with native wildlife, although the disruption caused by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] conquest of the world during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] introduced non-native creatures like [[Roggwart/Legends|roggwarts]] to the environment.<ref name="GAW" /> Still, Tirahnn was most well-known for its large, multi-tiered cities, the largest of which&mdash;also named [[Tirahnn (city)|Tirahnn]]&mdash;stretched for hundreds of miles in all directions. The second world from its [[Tirahnn (star)|sun]], Tirahnn had nine [[Moon/Legends|moons]], and had a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] lasting 272 [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of 28 [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] each.<ref name="tt" />

==History==
{{Quote|The planet you see before you is Tirahnn, a world on the Perlemian Trade Route. Some months ago, the planet fell into Separatist hands, and we could not spare the resources to oppose them. Since that time, the Separatists have used their control of the world to disrupt trade and supply lines, and the Jedi Council has tasked us with dislodging the Separatists and reopening the trade route.|Ezar Elasra|<ref name="GAW" />}}
As a stop along the one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] busiest [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]], the Perlemian Trade Route, Tirahnn developed a society highly influenced by trade. Tirahnn's bazaars and shops had became famous throughout the galaxy, and the world was known a stop for bargain-hunting, rich tourists who wanted a real-life street level experience.<ref name="tt" /> Tirahnn's location and status as a trade nexus made it a target for invasion at several points throughout its history: the world was [[Battle of Tirahnn (Tionese War)|taken]] by the [[Honorable Union of Desevro and Tion|Honorable Union of Desevro & Tion]] during the [[Tionese War]], during the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] early centuries.<ref name="Warfare" /> Tirahnn later sided with the Galactic Republic at the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], only to be conquered by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] in an effort to cut off a vital supply line down the Perlemian. The Separatists proceeded to heavily fortify Tirahnn, putting in place a powerful defense [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] around the planet and commandeering a [[planetary ion cannon]] located within Tirahnn city. Despite the disruption of trade with the Republic, the Confederacy allowed the markets to operate relatively normally, although [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] became a regular sight in the streets and [[IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tank/Legends|''Hailfire'' droid tanks]] were routinely used to dispel gatherings.<ref name="GAW" />

[[File:TirahnnChase.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Luke Skywalker and Leia Organa flee from Catuman warriors on Tirahnn.]]
Several months later, the Republic launched a mission to retake the world, led by the [[Barabel/Legends|Barabel]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ezar Elasra]]. The [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] carried this out by sneaking a team of commandos onto Tirahnn via a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/stealth/Legends|LAAT/s stealth gunship]], and after a crash landing that claimed the lives of several [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], sabotaging the [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] and clearing the way for a [[Battle of Tirahnn (Clone Wars)|full-fledged invasion]]. The Republic operatives proceeded to lead a successful ambush of a major Confederate tank convoy, cutting off one of their main lines of retreat and leading to a decisive Republic victory.<ref name="GAW" /> By the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the world was governed by a mercantile oligarchy ruled by Tirahnn's richest merchant princes, who periodically chose one of their own to hold an honorary [[Governor/Legends|governor]] position. The Empire maintained a light presence on Tirahnn, occasionally sending delegations to visit the sitting governor. The criminal organization known as the [[Osaji Syndicate]] made major inroads on Tirahnn during the [[Rebellion era]], with Osaji higher-up [[Osaji Varane]] operating a successful import-export business on the world.<ref name="tt" />

In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], Tirahnn was visited by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] leaders [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], when Solo's ''[[Millennium Falcon/Legends|Millennium Falcon]]'' touched down on the world for supplies during the bustling [[Great Fair]]. Amidst the crowd, Skywalker and Organa had a run-in with the dangerous [[S'kytri]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Kharys]], who sent a team of [[Catuman]] warriors chasing the Rebels through the streets. Solo&mdash;the real target of Kharys' hunt&mdash;saved them and brought them back to the ''Falcon'', only for Kharys to
[[Death/Legends|kill]] Solo's friend [[Katya M'Buele]] with a [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[Smoke Demon|smoke demon]]. Desiring revenge, Solo and his friends left Tirahnn to defeat Kharys on her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Skye]].<ref name="hunt" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|All my life, I've heard tales of the Great Tirahnn Fair, but I never thought I'd get to visit it.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="hunt" />}}
Sixty percent of Tirahnn's 9 billion inhabitants were [[Human/Legends|Humans]], but many [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] called the Inner Rim planet home. The planet's unrelentingly capitalist society led to a stark social stratification and a large wealth gap: Tirahnn's elite, who lived in the ornate skyscrapers of [[the Heights]], would sometimes boast that their feet had not touched the ground in decades. Owing to Tirahnn's lacking law enforcement infrastructure, few of Tirahnn's richest natives left their homes without armed backup. The Great Fair, which stretched throughout Tirahnn's mild summer,<ref name="tt" /> also brought many offworld visitors to Tirahnn. Among the frequent visitors were the winged S'kytri of Skye, who previously were only rarely seen away from their clan holdings.<ref name="gamer">{{GamerCite|1|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Marvel Series}}</ref> The arrival of the Separatists during the Clone Wars also provided a large infusion of new blood from offworld, which at times came at the expense of the natives: for instance, when the [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrian]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Zolghast]] commandeered a police outpost in Tirahnn city's main financial district to serve as his operational center, all of the police working out of the building lost their jobs.<ref name="GAW" />

==Locations==
Tirahnn's largest city, also called Tirahnn, consisted of hundreds of miles of seemingly endless bazaars that extended as much upwards as it did across the planet's landscape. Tirahnn was divided into many different levels, with the street level primarily being inhabited by craftsmen and traders, and the planet's elite residing above in skyscrapers that rose [[Meter/Legends|kilometers]] above the ground. Most of Tirahnn's richest inhabitants lived in a posh neighborhood known as the Heights, which was populated by palatial towers. Tirahnn's mercantilist culture was seen all over the planet, not just in its large cities, as even the smallest village was built around a bazaar. Some of Tirahnn's famous markets could be the size of entire nations on other worlds, and almost anything outside of serious military equipment could be found somewhere within. They also resulted in a lax approach towards law enforcement, as the merchant princes recognized that it was nearly impossible to prevent petty crime in such an environment.<ref name="tt" />

==Behind the scenes==
Tirahnn first appeared in [[Star Wars Annual (1977) 1|''Star Wars Annual'' (1977) 1]], written by [[Chris Claremont]] and released in [[1979]].<ref name="hunt" /> Extensive information on the planet was later given in the [[Wizards of the Coast]] adventure scenario ''[[Triplet Threat]]'',<ref name="tt" /> and it was the site of an example campaign in the [[2009]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' sourcebook ''[[Galaxy at War]]''.<ref name="GAW" /> Tirahnn was reintroduced in the newer [[Canon]] timeline in [[2015]], when it was mentioned in [[Jason Fry]]'s junior novel ''[[Servants of the Empire: Rebel in the Ranks]]''.<ref name="rebel">''[[Servants of the Empire: Rebel in the Ranks]]''</ref>
